features: THE ONES WHO ARRIVED LATER — This version touches the database: two migrations. The first records who modifies a communication, a ticket or a document — until now only the creator was known. The second creates the three new notification preferences for existing users, giving each the state of its «new» sibling: those who receive new communications will also receive updates, those who had them off stay off.

SOMEONE ADDED TO A COMMUNICATION NEVER RECEIVED IT. EVER. The forum asked for modifications to be notified too, but underneath there were two different things and nobody had reported the first: recipients were fixed at creation time, so anyone added later in an edit — a building, an owner — received nothing, neither then nor ever. The communication existed and they only saw it by going and looking. Now whoever enters the audience receives it, and receives it as new, because for them it is. This holds for notice board communications, maintenance tickets and archive documents.

FOR TICKETS THE SHAPE IS DIFFERENT: their audience is not a chosen list, it is the building. The case where it changes is moving the ticket to another building, and from then on it concerns people who knew nothing about it. The list of owners that can also be filled in does not decide who gets the notification, and it was not made to: it would have sent mail to people the creation never mails.

AND THEN THE ACTUAL MODIFICATION, WITH A CHECKBOX. Notifying on every save would have meant emailing the whole building because a comma was fixed. In the edit form there is therefore a checkbox — off every time the form opens — that sends a notice to those who had already received the communication. The last word stays with whoever signs it. They are two different notices and not the same one worded differently: telling someone «new communication» about something they have already read would be false, and the second time they would stop opening them.

THREE NEW SWITCHES IN THE PREFERENCES, AND TWO BUTTONS. Update notifications have their own preference, separate from the one for new things: you can keep being told about new communications and not about every correction. There are three — notice board, tickets, archive — and every role that already saw the matching «new» ones sees them, owners included. With fourteen switches on the page, and more to come, above the list there are now «Enable all» and «Disable all» with a count of how many are on: they do not save, they change the page, and saving stays the button it always was.

THE NOTICE NOW SAYS WHO ACTUALLY MADE THE CHANGE. The tables only recorded who created: an update notice naming that person would say something false about who did what, in an email that reaches the whole building. Now the column exists and the notice writes «was updated by …» with the right name. It matters beyond the email too: in a practice with several people, «who changed this communication after it was published?» is a question that comes up sooner or later, and until now it had no answer anywhere.

A DOCUMENT NO LONGER FAILS TO DOWNLOAD WHEN ITS TITLE CONTAINS A SLASH. From the forum: after changing a document's name the download started giving the generic error, and restoring the old name made it work again. The reporter's own diagnosis was exact: a character not allowed in a file name — in their case «/» — made the download fail. ⚠️ The title was not forbidden, and that is the part that matters: «Verbale 12/2026» is a correct title — in Italy minutes are numbered that way. Only the file name changes, becoming «Verbale 12-2026.pdf»; in the archive the title stays what you wrote. Fixed along with it the other characters a file name does not accept, which did not break the download but prevented the file from being saved on Windows.

CO-OWNERS: A QUESTION WE ANSWERED, NOT A DEFECT. An administrator asked how to keep the register correct with several owners without the «trick» of giving 100% to one and zero to the others. He is right, and that trick is exactly what should not be done: the data is also used for the owners' register and for meeting notices. The answer is a feature already designed — an accounting weight separate from the register share, plus a switch deciding who appears in allocations — and it arrives in a later version. It was not improvised here.

UNDER THE HOOD: the same shape had recurred for three versions — the manual allocation that «only came from the form at creation» and the account capacity check «wired only at creation» were the two precedents. Now an automated check demands that whoever notifies someone at creation has decided what to do on modification: either it does, or it states in writing why not. It does not impose symmetry, it imposes the choice. Another check verifies that every notification type has a label and a description in all four languages: with three new types that was twenty-four entries written by hand, and one forgotten would show English in the middle of an Italian page with no error to flag it.
